label: Length-3 first copy step after <DEL> (outputting token 1), plus weak t=0 firing on g/y/0
explanation: Two-part but simple position-based unit. (1) Strong component (~61% of activation mass, nearly all top activations): in length-3 sequences at step 4, the first copy step after <DEL> where the model outputs original token 1; active on ~46% of such steps, with magnitude up to the max. (2) Weak, near-deterministic component (~35% of mass, ~78% of active steps): step 0 when the first token is y, g, or 0 (fires on essentially all of those). Magnitude here is small: y ~0.10 of max, 0 ~0.04, g near threshold. Residual: weak firing at step 5 (recall_idx 2 for L=3, recall_idx 1 for L=4). It never fires at the delimiter step, at original positions 1+, or at copy steps beyond recall_idx 2. Activation does not depend on which token is being copied or on digit count. Dev: P 0.97, R 0.96, F1 0.97, mass recall 0.96.

issues: Factual error in the explanation: the unit is NOT active on 'about 46%' of the L=3, recall_idx=1 steps. On test, (L==3)&(recall_idx==1) has precision 0.858 (2604 predicted). On dev, 2286 of about 2605 such steps are active, roughly 88%. So the claim understates the rate by about half. The other numbers hold: this component carries 0.61 of the mass and almost all top-quartile activations.

t=0 component checks out. g, y and 0 each have precision 1.0 at t=0. Together they give recall 0.79 (claimed 78%) and mass 0.354 (claimed 35%). g carries almost no mass (0.005). y carries 0.246 and 0 carries 0.103, which fits the stated ordering of magnitudes.
Token independence checks out. For L=3 recall1, precision is 0.861 when the output is a digit and 0.857 when it is a letter. The inactive steps (about 12%) show no visible token pattern.

Residual checks out and is small: misses hold 3.9% of mass, all at step 5. Most are L=3 recall_idx 2 (precision 0.156, mass 0.034). L=4 recall_idx 1 is very rare (precision 0.007, mass 0.005), so calling it part of the residual slightly overstates it.
Zero firing at the delimiter, at original positions 1 and later, and at t>=6 is confirmed by the profile.

No systematic false-positive or missed class remains. Test precision 0.971, recall 0.96, F1 0.966 are reproduced. Adding (t==5)&(L<=4) only lowers precision (F1 0.60), so the current predicate is close to optimal.
